transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Um… I guess I’m here because flying has been feeling a lot scarier than it should. Even just thinking about getting on a plane, I start picturing this really bad turbulence from my honeymoon flight. I know people fly safely all the time, but… it still gets to me.
Is it mainly flying that worries you, or do you feel anxious in other situations too, like public speaking or being in crowded places?

Mostly flying. I don’t really think of myself as anxious in general… it’s just the plane thing. Even thinking about getting on one brings back that rough honeymoon flight, the turbulence and all that. I know flying is supposed to be safe, but it still bothers me.
When you think about getting on a plane, does the anxiety ever happen in other situations that remind you of flying, or is it pretty much limited only to air travel?

It’s mostly tied to flying, yeah. But even things that remind me of it can set it off… like if I’m looking up flights for a work conference, or I hear a plane go over, my chest tightens pretty quickly. I kind of just want to close the laptop or stop thinking about it.
Does this fear of flying ever lead you to avoid certain trips or opportunities, or does it cause a lot of distress that affects your daily life?

Yeah… it does, a bit. I’ve picked really long drives instead of flying, and I’ve turned down a couple work trainings because they involved a flight. If I have to even talk through a trip, I usually need my husband there with me, or I start wanting to back out.
Have you ever experienced sudden episodes of intense fear or physical symptoms like rapid heartbeat, sweating, or shortness of breath in situations that aren’t related to flying?
Not really… I mean, I don’t think so. I can get stressed like anyone, but those intense fear feelings are pretty much when it has to do with flying.
When you're exposed to flying-related triggers, like looking up flights or hearing a plane overhead, do you almost always experience an immediate panic attack or intense fear reaction?
Yeah… pretty much right away. If I’m looking at flights or hear a plane, my chest tightens and I get this rush of panic. I just want to shut it down or get away from thinking about it.
